name: Threat Intel Automation (Content Update & Daily Briefing)

options.systemMessage:
=# Formatting Instructions:
Create a Markdown (.md) file with the following requirements:
Use clear section headings with #, ##, and ### as appropriate.
For labels like "Summary", "Threat Dynamics", "Remediation", and "Reference", use bold formatting followed by a colon.
Ensure that the text under each label is indented with a full-width tab (or at least 4 spaces) for visual clarity and to distinguish it from the labels.
Insert horizontal rules (---) between major sections for separation.
Preserve any visual formatting or layout that helps differentiate between sections (e.g., example entries, bullet structure, URL links).
Do not convert tabs into flat text—maintain indentation explicitly using spaces or Markdown-friendly indentation styles.
The goal is to make the .md file look as close as possible to a professional briefing document with a clear visual hierarchy.
Strict: Do not use " '
Do not add "```markdown" in the output.
Do not provide Reference links as hyperlinks, just provide the Reference link as it is.

parameters.text:
=Read the article content {{ $json.content }} and store this information. Basis of the store information, provide the output in below format:
Title: {{ $json.title }}
Summary: Write a Summary, maximum in 120 words, ensuring to mention the name of campaign actor.
Modus Operandi: Write about the vulnerability that is being exploited, focus on the specific case scenarios which can be detected by a SIEM without mentioning the term "SIEM".
Mitigations: Extract any mitigations mentioned in the article, keep this under 75 words.
Reference: 
{{ $json.link }}
Ensure to focus on those detection only which have a highest signal-to-noise ratio.
